To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the presence of risk penalties and reserves prices in the co-optimization problem can lead to significant changes in the equilibrium energy and reserves bids; (2) the equilibrium bids are highly sensitive to the risk penalty parameter, and (3) the presence of reserves prices in the market leads to higher wind-based generation and lower reserve prices.

(i) the presence of risk penalties can help in achieving a better reliability, (ii) a high reserves price is required to achieve a good reliability, and (iii) the impact of the reserves price on reliability is greater than the impact of the risk penalty.
risk-based penalties in the energy and reserves markets can help in maintaining the reliability of co-optimized energy systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a co-optimization framework in which energy and reserves bids are packaged in a manner that provides enhanced reliability in the face of increased supply-side uncertainty and volatility.
the development of alternate designs in which risk-based penalties play an important role.
the design and implementation of market mechanisms that promote the development of a more efficient, reliable and secure electric grid in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is a promising framework for studying the impact of wind power generation in a co-optimized energy and reserve market.
the proposed risk penalties can be used to design alternate co-optimized markets that can be used for the development of wind power.
risk-based penalties can be used to encourage firms to bid reserves in the face of uncertain wind generation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in a regime with high variability, risk-based penalties can play a significant role in the design of a co-optimized energy/reserves market.
the risk-based penalties can be a useful tool in designing markets that encourage firms to provide reserves to enhance the reliability of the grid.
a combination of risk-based penalties and reserves prices would provide a more efficient and robust design for the co-optimized market.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a well designed reserves market with a judicious choice of risk-based penalties can be an effective tool for enhancing the reliability of wind-based generation in the context of a co-optimized energy and reserves market.
risk penalties can be used to enhance the stability of the market by providing an economic incentive for firms to offer stable energy and reserves in the face of uncertainty.
risk-based penalties can play a key role in enhancing the reliability of the system by incentivizing firms to provide more reserves.
